vorhaben.titel: The sidebar widget suits dark sites
vorhaben.satz: Three colour schemes for [naws_weather_widget]: light as before, dark for dark sidebars, and transparent — then the widget draws no card and takes its text and line colours from the sidebar. Set under Appearance, with a preview on a dark ground, or per placement with scheme="dark" on the shortcode.

vorhaben.titel: A year of daily means as a calendar
vorhaben.satz: [naws_heatmap] shows a year of daily mean temperatures as a grid: months down, days across, one coloured tile per day, and buttons for the years. What a curve makes you read, the grid lets you see — the cold fortnight in February, the hot week in July. The colour scale is a setting, and on a phone the month column stays put while the days scroll beneath it.

The interface no longer relies on the plugin's own language files but on the route WordPress provides for every plugin. Anyone can contribute a language on translate.wordpress.org without touching a line of code, and every language gets a proper language pack. German and Norwegian are complete.

The plugin no longer has a language setting of its own. It follows the site language and, where the profile says so, the language of the logged-in user. Your back end can be in one language and your visitors' pages in another, which was impossible before. If you used the old setting, set the site language once instead.

vorhaben.titel: Weekdays, months and weather conditions speak along
vorhaben.satz: They were hardcoded lists in German and English; a Norwegian reader got English with no way to change it. They are ordinary translatable strings now, and the short date is a format string rather than a branch — a language that writes its dates the other way round can say so.

vorhaben.titel: The table shortcode does what it promises
vorhaben.satz: [naws_table] shows readings as a table over a period, grouped by hour, day, week, month or year. The shortcode had always been documented and listed, but the template file it includes was missing — it returned an empty page. The recommended periods such as 24h and 30d are read correctly now as well.

vorhaben.titel: The modules' identifiers stay on the server
vorhaben.satz: Netatmo addresses a module by its MAC address, and that address used to be written into every page carrying a live dashboard or a history chart. What travels now is a public name such as outdoor or indoor, which the server resolves back. Pages cached before the change keep working unchanged.

vorhaben.titel: The bundled language files are read
vorhaben.satz: German and Norwegian travel with the plugin as files, so an installation does not have to wait for its language pack. In 1.9.9 WordPress silently refused both — a mistake in the file header, with no warning, just English text. They are read now, and the translations that had gone missing in the move are back.

vorhaben.titel: One shortcode for twenty-seven computed values
vorhaben.satz: Dew point, apparent temperature, frost days and summer days, degree-day sums and the SPI drought index — all through a single shortcode, with not one figure worked out by hand.

vorhaben.titel: A short outage at Netatmo no longer costs a reading
vorhaben.satz: When the Netatmo service reports that it is busy, the plugin waits exactly as long as the server asks and then asks again — instead of writing a gap into the series.

vorhaben.titel: The encryption speaks up when it is not working
vorhaben.satz: A new status panel shows whether your credentials really are stored encrypted — and names the four reasons that can stop it from happening.

vorhaben.titel: Header colour and typeface are settings now
vorhaben.satz: The dark header bars and the font in use are picked on the appearance screen, instead of having to be hunted down in a stylesheet.

vorhaben.titel: The API key belongs in the header, not in the address bar
vorhaben.satz: The REST API accepts the key in the X-NAWS-Key header only. A secret in the address bar is written down by access logs, the Referer header, the browser history and every cache along the way. Calls using ?api_key= answer 401 from now on — if you use the API, switch over before you update.
Live cards and yearly comparisons can be dragged into place in the settings — and the list shows only what your page actually carries: switch a module off and its cards go with it.
